summary: The line "Suffering is incomprehensible" tells you how stripped-down and severe this is. People love it for the spiritual crisis, the chill in every frame, and how hard it stares at doubt without softening it.
good_pick_if: you want a short, intense drama that leaves room for silence
maybe_skip_if: you want comfort, warmth, or easy answers

summary: That review saying this "is not" just a boy-and-bird story is exactly the point. It is tender and rough at the same time, with a small pocket of freedom set against a life that keeps closing in.
good_pick_if: you want something humane, grounded, and quietly devastating
maybe_skip_if: you want escape instead of social reality

source_quotes.text: A story about a boy training a kestrel during his free time, this is not.

summary: One great read on it calls these "fundamentally decent people" struggling with things others cannot understand, which is why it still lands so hard: generous, adult, and full of earned feeling.
good_pick_if: you want a big classic that feels emotionally generous, not dusty
maybe_skip_if: you want cynicism or a faster modern rhythm

source_quotes.text: fundamentally decent people who are having a tough time

summary: The "good cry" reputation is earned, but the bigger sell is the sheer storybook sweep of it. It feels like somebody turned imagination itself into a fantasy epic and left the sadness intact.
good_pick_if: you want something visually huge and emotionally soft at the edges
maybe_skip_if: you want fantasy driven more by rules than feeling

source_quotes.text: the most perfect movie for when you need a good cry

summary: Even the joking "build a bridge with the boys" review gets at how watchable the movie makes obsession. It is grand, procedural, and tense in a way that turns engineering pride into real drama.
good_pick_if: you want an old-school epic with brains as well as scale
maybe_skip_if: you want war movies to move faster or stay less formal

source_quotes.text: love to build a bridge with the boys

summary: "Absolute hypnosis" is a good way to describe it. The movie turns line delivery, jazz, and courtroom maneuvering into something so rhythmically alive that the long runtime barely registers.
good_pick_if: you want a legal drama carried by talk, texture, and tension
maybe_skip_if: you want neat moral certainty or blunt pacing

summary: That "Get yourself buried" line captures the entire mood: corrosive dialogue, nasty charisma, and a New York nightscape so sharp and poisonous you almost want to stay in it longer.
good_pick_if: you want something ruthless, stylish, and very quotable
maybe_skip_if: you want even one genuinely comforting person onscreen

source_quotes.text: You’re dead son. Get yourself buried.

summary: The joke about getting picked on and deciding to "become the Emperor of France" fits because this is an insanely ambitious silent epic that treats history like a playground for formal invention and giant feeling.
good_pick_if: you want a classic that feels huge, playful, and formally alive
maybe_skip_if: you want historical drama in a compact package

summary: Calling it the "quickest 3 hours ever" makes sense once it gets moving. It is an emotional avalanche: huge performances, overlapping ache, and maximalist filmmaking that somehow keeps the whole mess alive.
good_pick_if: you want a sprawling drama that goes all the way big
maybe_skip_if: you want subtlety, restraint, or emotional distance

source_quotes.text: Quite possibly the quickest 3 hours ever.

summary: That "not good fellas" joke is one way into a movie that plays less like a swagger piece and more like a haunted memory. It is sprawling, melancholy, and heavy with regret the whole way through.
good_pick_if: you want a gangster epic that feels bruised rather than triumphant
maybe_skip_if: you want cleaner pacing or less heaviness

source_quotes.text: these men were most definitely not good fellas
